summary: Active II has agreement with ʕam-/aʕm- partner and ʕal matter, versus success-giving with a causer and recipient. Detransitive expresses success without an external causee.
The three divine-success passages justify one lexical sense across marriage and return from an undertaking; the wedding object may additionally suggest compatibility but is not split.
62/340 is semantic success evidence, while its precise box is unresolved; German past or result interpretation alone cannot prove Preterit morphology.

Active mwafqile with God as l-agent immediately precedes agentless plural mwafqi at Jan 1.21/974. This is unusually direct evidence for the active grant-success versus Detransitive succeed opposition already recognized in round 1.

Repeated mwafəq/mwafqi and first-person mwafaqno support a Detransitive Preterit box that round 1 left unresolved at 62/340. Some predicates may still be lexical successful descriptions; do not infer the morphological box from the English perfect alone.

The counterfactual gəd miwafaqwo establishes Detransitive Infectum-wa. Agreement/consent and success should not be conflated solely on the common wfq consonants. No new light-verb collocation is established here.
Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses rest on the Turoyo; any English quoted below is copied from that supplied translation.
62/340: verify mwafəq as Detransitive Preterit versus an unmarked Infectum before adding a new box.
JTM 1.3/3: verify the suffix segmentation in kəmwafaqqe and the balance between granting success and making the couple compatible.

Confirm whether Jan’s unprefixed mwafəq/mwafqi/mwafaqno form a productive Detransitive Preterit paradigm or include lexical successful predicates; the first-person and failed-event contexts favor the proposed box.
Is Məwafəq yo at Jan 2.31/4927 an Arabic loan adjective acceptable, an agreement response, or a productive Part act.? No box is added from it.
Confirm patient -i- plus agent -le in mwafqile and the optative -lox segmentation in mwafaqlox.
Jan independently supports round-1 divine success-giving, with negated plural affected participants and optative second-person singular/plural suffixes. No new sense is proposed.
The inherited Detransitive success sense applies to a society in national struggle, alongside individual legal, interview and computer work. This is a participant/domain extension.
